query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Maintain and review a Notion-based project task page and append-only log for a technical project, including reading state, posting review/decision rows, updating task-page checklists, and inspecting a Supabase schema to support implementation decisions.
query_ground_truth.intent: Examine the Supabase schema structure to gather technical context required for implementation decisions.

requirement_groups.purpose: inspect supabase database schema and structure

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if project reference unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Identify the target project using SUPABASE_LIST_ALL_PROJECTS (select the intended project reference for downstream calls).
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Enumerate schemas/tables/views using SUPABASE_LIST_TABLES (build inventory from response.data.schemas[].tables[].full_name, not a flat tables list).
[Required] [Step]: Fetch columns/types/primary keys/relationships using SUPABASE_GET_TABLE_SCHEMAS (pass schema-qualified table_names; batch small, e.g., <=20 per call, and retry only failed tables).

[Fallback (if inventory/details are empty, partial, or truncated/previewed)] [Fallback]: Backfill/verify tables/columns/constraints/relationships using SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY (query system catalogs for authoritative metadata).
[Optional (if validating data-level shape)] [Next Step]: Spot-check a few rows using SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE (explicit select + small LIMIT to confirm nullability/types match metadata).

[Optional (if you need generated types for application code)] [Next Step]: Generate typed definitions using SUPABASE_GENERATE_TYPESCRIPT_TYPES (cross-check key tables against SUPABASE_GET_TABLE_SCHEMAS output).
known_pitfalls: [SUPABASE_LIST_TABLES] response.data.tables can be null while objects exist under response.data.schemas[].tables[]; also watch response.data.query_metadata.errors (e.g., HTTP 502/544) for incomplete inventory.

[SUPABASE_GET_TABLE_SCHEMAS] Large multi-table requests can return truncated or preview-only payloads and/or per-table failures (e.g., "Unauthorized"); retry only failed table_names in smaller batches.
[SUPABASE_GET_TABLE_SCHEMAS] foreign_keys commonly use source_column/target_schema/target_table/target_column; assuming different field names breaks relationship mapping.

[SUPABASE_SELECT_FROM_TABLE] Missing required "select" can error; complex expressions may 400 (failed to parse select) and schema-qualified resolution can 404 (schema cache)—use SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY for complex SQL.
[SUPABASE_RUN_READ_ONLY_QUERY] Catalog queries may legitimately return zero rows when schemas contain no user objects; treat as empty inventory, not an execution failure.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Parse SUPABASE_GET_TABLE_SCHEMAS payload(s), summarize tables, and derive FK edges using observed foreign_keys field names (handle data_preview vs data).

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: Supabase is an open-source backend-as-a-service providing a Postgres database, authentication, storage, and real-time subscription APIs for building modern applications
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=supabase. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="supabase") to create a connection BEFORE executing any supabase tools.

SUPABASE_LIST_TABLES.description: Lists all tables and views in specified database schemas, providing a quick overview of database structure to help identify available tables before fetching detailed schemas.

schemas.description: List of schemas to search for tables (maximum 10). If not provided, lists tables from all non-system schemas. Specify schema names to limit the search to specific schemas.

project_ref.description: The unique reference ID of the Supabase project. Must be exactly 20 lowercase letters (a-z only, no numbers or hyphens). This is visible in your Supabase project URL (e.g., https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/{project_ref}).

include_views.description: Whether to include views along with tables in the results

include_metadata.description: Whether to include basic metadata like estimated row count and table size

include_system_schemas.description: Whether to include system schemas (pg_catalog, information_schema, etc.) when listing all schemas. When set to false, temporary and internal schemas such as pg_temp_*, pg_toast_temp_* and pgbouncer are excluded from the results.

SUPABASE_GET_TABLE_SCHEMAS.description: Retrieves column details, types, and constraints for multiple database tables to help debug schema issues and write accurate SQL queries. Use the SUPABASE_LIST_TABLES action first to discover available tables, the fetch their detailed schemas.

project_ref.description: The unique reference ID of the Supabase project. This is visible in your Supabase project URL (e.g., https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/{project_ref}).

table_names.description: List of table names to retrieve schemas for. At least one table name is required (empty lists are not allowed). Tables can be from different schemas (e.g., 'public.users', 'operations.call_queue_items'). Without schema prefix, 'public' is assumed. Maximum 20 tables per request.

include_indexes.description: Whether to include index information in the response

exclude_null_values.description: Whether to exclude properties with null values from the response for cleaner output

include_relationships.description: Whether to include foreign key relationships in the response

SUPABASE_LIST_ALL_PROJECTS.description: Retrieves a list of all Supabase projects, including their ID, name, region, and status, for the authenticated user. Authentication: - Requires a valid Bearer token in the Authorization header. - Token format: 'Bearer <access_token>' where access_token is either: - A Personal Access Token (PAT) generated from https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens - An OAuth2 access token with the 'Projects.Read' scope Required Scope: - Projects.Read: Allows retrieval of project metadata. Returns: List of Project objects containing id, name, organization_id, region, status, database info, and created_at.
